transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... well, I've been having some trouble at work lately. I've been avoiding my clients and... skipping presentations. It's... it's because of my face. My mouth and my jaw. 

There's this droop, and it's uneven. I just... I can't stop seeing it in every mirror or photo. Other people tell me it looks fine, but... it's just really obvious to me. So... that's why I'm here, I guess.
Do you find yourself constantly thinking about the appearance of your mouth and jaw?
Yes. It's... it's pretty much all I think about. Like I said, I can't stop seeing the droop and the unevenness. Every reflection... every photo. It just consumes my thoughts.
Has your concern about the appearance of your mouth and jaw interfered with your relationships or daily activities?

Yeah... I suppose it has. Um... I actually cancelled a major client presentation recently, right at the last minute. I just... I couldn't face being seen. 

And there's some networking for an award that I've been skipping. I just stay home. Um... my project deadlines are kind of falling apart because of it. And... I guess I've been avoiding family gatherings, too. I just... I don't want to be around people right now.
Is your concern only about the appearance of your mouth and jaw, or do you also worry about other parts of your body?
Um... no. Just... just my mouth and jaw. That's... that's the only thing.
Do you think that other people can see the droop and unevenness in your mouth and jaw?

Um... sometimes people will tell me I look fine, but... yes. It just feels so obvious to me. That's... that's why I can't face the clients or do those presentations anymore. I just feel like they must be looking at it.
Do you find yourself repeating certain actions over and over, like checking your appearance in the mirror, in an attempt to cope with your concerns about your mouth and jaw?

Um... yes. I suppose I do. Before work... or if I actually go to a family event... I can be in the bathroom for hours. Just... checking the mirror. 

I take a lot of pictures on my phone, too. From different angles. And I just keep redoing my makeup... or adjusting my scarf to try and hide it. 

I ask my husband if my face looks lopsided. Probably too much. And... I don't know, I just scroll through photos of other women online. Just to see how bad mine looks compared to theirs. So... yeah. I do that a lot.
How much distress do you feel when you think about the appearance of your mouth and jaw?
Um... a lot, I guess. It just... it really bothers me. It's hard to think about anything else sometimes.
Have you had to take time off work or school specifically because of your concerns about your mouth and jaw?

Um... yes. I've missed some things. 

I... I actually cancelled a major client presentation recently. Just at the last minute. I couldn't do it. And there are these networking events for awards that I've been skipping. I just... I can't face being seen by all those people. 

My project deadlines are slipping, too. And... I haven't been going to family gatherings much either. It's just... getting harder to manage everything.
Do you think that your perception of the droop and unevenness in your mouth and jaw might be exaggerated or not entirely accurate?
No. I... I don't think so. I mean, I see what I see in the mirror. It's right there. I'm not... I'm not making it up.
Have you ever had a time when you didn't think your mouth and jaw looked uneven or droopy?
I... I'm not really sure. Maybe a long time ago, but... I don't know. I can't really remember it being any different.
Have you experienced any difficulties in your relationships with friends or family members because of your concerns about your mouth and jaw?

I... I think I mentioned this already. I haven't been going to family gatherings. And... well, work is suffering too, like I said about the presentation and the networking events. It's just... I can't be around people right now. Everything's just sort of falling apart.
Have you ever thought that maybe your mouth and jaw don't look as uneven or droopy as you think they do?
I... didn't you just ask me that? No. I... I know what I look like. It's not just in my head.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your mouth and jaw might look different to you at different times?
No. It's... it's always the same. I don't see how it would change.
Have you noticed any significant problems in your relationships with your husband or other family members because of your concerns about your mouth and jaw?

I... I feel like we just went over this. Like I said, the family gatherings are falling apart because I just won't go. And with my husband... it's just hard. 

Everything is. I told you about work... I ended up canceling a major client presentation at the very last minute. I've been missing all the award networking events because I just... I can't face being seen by anyone looking like this. So my project deadlines, my family... it's all just falling apart.
Have you lost a job or been unable to start one because of your concerns about your mouth and jaw?

I... I feel like I just answered this. I haven't been fired yet, if that's what you're asking. 

But like I just said... I canceled that major client presentation. I'm missing all the networking events because I just can't let anyone see me. My project deadlines are falling apart. So... I don't know how much longer I can keep my job when everything is just... slipping away like this.
Have you ever had a period of time where your concerns about your mouth and jaw lessened or went away?
No. Not really. It's... it's always there. I don't think it's ever just... gone away.
Are there any other areas of your life, besides work and family gatherings, that you feel are being negatively impacted by your concerns about your mouth and jaw?

I... I don't really know what else you want me to say. I feel like we just keep going over the same things. 

It's... it's just what I already told you. The major client presentations I had to cancel, missing the award networking because I just can't face being seen... the project deadlines and the family gatherings falling apart. That's pretty much my whole life right there. I don't really go anywhere or do anything else. So... no. Just that.
Do you think your mouth and jaw look worse at certain times than at others?
I don't know. No... I don't think so. It just always looks the way it does. I haven't really noticed it changing or being worse on certain days. It's just... always bad.
Do you worry that your appearance will cause others to think you're unattractive or that there's something seriously wrong with your health?

I don't... I don't really know what other people are thinking. I just know I don't want them looking at me. I haven't really thought about the health thing, if that's what you mean. It's just... I know how it looks. And I just don't want to be seen.
